source_text: Ἐρεῖς οὖν μοι· Σὺ φῂς τὸν θεὸν ἐν τόπῳ μὴ δεῖν χωρεῖσθαι, καὶ πῶς νῦν λέγεις αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ περιπατεῖν; Ἄκουε ὅ φημι. Ὁ μὲν θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τῶν ὅλων ἀχώρητός ἐστιν καὶ ἐν τόπῳ οὐχ εὑρίσκεται· οὐ γάρ ἐστιν τόκος τῆς καταπαύσεως αὐτοῦ. Ὁ δὲ λόγος αὐτοῦ, δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα πεποίηκεν, δύναμις ὢν καὶ σοφία αὐτοῦ, ἀναλαμβάνων τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου τῶν ὅλων, οὗτος παρεγίνετο εἰς τὸν· παράδεισον ἐν προσώπῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ὡμίλει τῷ Ἀδάμ.
pass_a_gloss: You will say to me: You say God ought not to be contained in a place, and how now do you say Him walking in the paradise? Hear what I say. God and Father of all is not contained in a place and is not found in a place; for rest of Him is not a product. But the Word of Him, through whom all things have been made, being power and wisdom of Him, taking the person of the Father and Lord of all, this One came into the paradise in the person of God and spoke to Adam.
pass_b_english: You will object: "You claim God cannot be contained in a place, so how can you now say He walked in the garden?" Listen to my answer. God the Father of all is uncontainable and cannot be located in any place, for no place can serve as His resting place. But His Word, through whom all things were made, who is His power and wisdom, took on the person of the Father and Lord of all; this One entered the garden in the person of God and spoke with Adam.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both accurately reflect the Greek text. Pass A is a more literal translation of the syntax, while Pass B provides a more fluent rendering. Both correctly handle the theological distinction between the uncontainable Father and the Word (Logos) who entered paradise. The translation of 'τόκος τῆς καταπαύσεως' as 'product of His rest' (Pass A) or 'no place can serve as His resting place' (Pass B) captures the sense of the Greek regarding the lack of a spatial limit for God's rest.
